newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude markets quiet, Brent softer.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude markets quiet, Brent softer.

text.p: North Sea crude oil markets were very quiet on Tuesday with little action reported on either the physical or paper markets, traders said.
"I've cleaned my desk and done my expenses for the first time in a year. That's how quiet it is," one large trader said.
Dated Brent traded Monday and Tuesday at June -28 cents for second decade May barrels, off Friday's deal at June -20 cents.

By 1740 GMT June Brent on the IPE futures had lost most of its earlier gains to trade up three cents at $18.00 a barrel. The contract was led to an intra-day high of $18.19 earlier on the back of strong NYMEX heating oil.
Both Brent dates were kept on Tuesday by Vitol and Esso. The cargoes are due to load in the May 21-23 period.
Talk that one trader had failed a VLCC destined for the U.S. Gulf was not seen as particularly market moving.
"The market is pretty well balanced in the short term. There are others looking at taking barrels over (to the U.S. Gulf) and the demand seems to be there," another trader said.
Brent intermonth spreads were untraded apart from an early Jun/Jul at -15 cents. In late talk May/June was bid at -24 cents while the best buyer on the Jul/Aug was seen at -16 cents.

Brent CFDs firmed slightly over the day but brokers emphasised that levels were notional. Next weeks' May 12-16 dates talked around June -26/-19 cents while the May 19-23 talked around June -18 cents.

While the Brent market remained dormant the Dubai paper market was relatively active. July Brent/Dubai traded at $1.03 and $1.05 a barrel while August moved at least once at $1.15 a barrel. Dubai Jul/Aug traded a few times around 6-7 cents while Aug/Sept moved at +5 cents.
